promptAsSent:
Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: Image 1: footprint, registration and material language only; do not copy its rotary barrels
Image 2: Image 2: material language only; do not copy its geometry

Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: production-source concept for one modular top-down tactical-game mech ARM weapon sprite
Primary request: a light machine gun for a mech arm: a short perforated barrel shroud on a narrow receiver with a flat box magazine lying along the top of the receiver and a small rear charging handle housing. Reads as a compact light support gun, clearly not a rotary chaingun and not the boxy belt-fed autogun. Image 1 supplies footprint, registration and material language only; do not copy its rotary barrel cluster. Image 2 supplies material language only; do not copy its geometry.
Critical perspective: strict 90-degree zenith orthographic top-down view. The camera looks straight down at the TOP surfaces of the weapon. The weapon fires horizontally toward the NORTH/TOP edge of the canvas, parallel to the battlefield plane. The muzzle faces AWAY from the camera, so the camera cannot see a circular bore, aperture face, dish, lens, or glowing front surface. At the extreme northmost tip show only a very thin, almost edge-on dark exit slit.
Style/medium: crisp high-resolution painted game sprite matching the existing modular mech weapon family: fine surface noise, panel seams, fasteners, restrained wear, upper-left baked object lighting, neutral olive-drab painted composite casing, dark gunmetal mechanisms, small amber service lamps. Composition/framing: exactly one isolated vertical module centred with generous padding on a flat featureless pure white isolation plate (no gradient, shadow, halo, floor, border or checkerboard). Symmetrical enough to mirror to either side. It is a LIGHT weapon: visibly smaller, simpler and lighter than the reference weapon, roughly 55 to 65 percent of the reference's width and 70 to 80 percent of its length, with a short rear mounting tab or plate that disappears beneath a mech chassis. Avoid: visible circular muzzle, upward-pointing barrel, perspective, isometric, side view, multiple objects, hands, mech body, vehicle, turret base, text, logo, watermark, cropping.
